Creating a Smile 
Across Every Mile
Positioned at the intersection of 
mobility, tourism, hospitality and 
digital services, IRCTC has built an 
integrated ecosystem that touches 
millions of lives every day. Through 
our diversified portfolio spanning 
Internet Ticketing, Catering, Tourism 
and Rail Neer, we create value across 
every touchpoint of the passenger 
journey. Whether i

ortfolio spanning 
Internet Ticketing, Catering, Tourism 
and Rail Neer, we create value across 
every touchpoint of the passenger 
journey. Whether it is simplifying 
access to travel through digital 
platforms, delivering quality hospitality 
onboard, curating memorable tourism 
experiences or ensuring the availability 
of safe drinking water, each of our 
businesses contributes to a reliable 
and customer-centric travel ecosystem.
This philosophy shaped our 
performance during FY2025-26. 
Driven by resilient growth across all 
four business verticals, disciplined 
execution and sustained operational 
excellence, IRCTC delivered its highest-
ever revenue, while also declaring the 
highest dividend in the Company’s 
history. More importantly, these 
achievements reflect the strength 
of a diversified business model that 
continues to create enduring value 
through operational resilience, digital 
innovation and customer trust.
India's travel and tourism ecosystem is undergoing a signi

ate enduring value 
through operational resilience, digital 
innovation and customer trust.
India's travel and tourism ecosystem is undergoing a significant 
transformation. Rapid digital adoption, sustained investments in railway and 
transport infrastructure, rising domestic tourism and evolving passenger 
expectations are redefining the way people travel. As mobility becomes 
increasingly connected and experience-driven, the opportunity extends 
beyond enabling journeys to enriching every stage of the travel experience.
As India’s travel economy continues to expand, IRCTC 
is uniquely positioned to support this growth by 
strengthening digital capabilities, expanding tourism 
offerings, enhancing passenger convenience and 
strengthening service excellence across its businesses. 
Every investment, innovation and service we deliver is 
guided by a singular purpose: creating greater value for 
passengers, partners, shareholders and the nation.

Chairman’s Message
Creating a Smile Across Every Mile
Dear Shareholders,
For over two and a half decades, IRCTC 
has played an integral role in India’s 
railway ecosystem, serving millions 
of passengers through hospitality, 
tourism, and digital ticketing. As 
the scale and aspirations of Indian 
travelers have grown, so too has our 
responsibility to enhance the passenger 
experience and create value across 
every mile of the journey.
This focus underpinned a landmark 
performance of IRCTC in FY 2025–26. 
IRCTC delivered its highest-ever 
financial results, with Revenue from 
Operations growing by 11.55% to 
₹5,215 crore (approx.). Profit before 
Tax stood at ₹1,875 crore, EBITDA 
increased by 8.30% to ₹1,926 crore 
and Profit after Tax stood at ₹1,393 
crore. Reflecting the strength of our 
performance and our commitment to 
shareholder value, the Board of IRCTC 
has recommended a final dividend 
of ₹0.50 per share, subject to the 
approval of the shareholders, taking 
the total div

r value, the Board of IRCTC 
has recommended a final dividend 
of ₹0.50 per share, subject to the 
approval of the shareholders, taking 
the total dividend per share to ₹9.00 
and total dividend payout for the 
year to ₹720 crore.
Delivering excellence across 
every mile
Each of our four business verticals 
delivered meaningful growth during FY 
2025-26, contributing to a resilient and 
well-balanced performance.
Catering remained our highest 
revenue-generating business recording 
an annual revenue of ₹2,399 crore and 
reflecting a growth of 12.88% over 
the previous year. We now serve close 
to 63 crore plus meals annually across 
approximately 1,450 plus passenger 
trains, supported by a network of 
more than 800 plus kitchens equipped 
with state of art equipment and AI-
enabled Quality Monitoring Systems. 
The E-Catering Business further 
expanded its reach to 420 plus railway 
stations, with 1.65 lakh plus average 
daily orders. During FY 2025-26, we 
also introduced E-Pantry ser

ther

stations, with 1.65 lakh plus average 
daily orders. During FY 2025-26, we 
also introduced E-Pantry services on a 
pilot basis across select Mail-Express 
trains, enabling passengers to pre-
book meals for seat-wise delivery; 
further enhancing service delivery and 
achieving customer delight through our 
digital hospitality platform.
In FY 2025-26, Rail Neer Package 
Drinking Water grossed a revenue of 
₹407crore approx., while profit grew by 
20.65% year-on-year. During the year, 
Rail Neer was also integrated with the 
E-Pantry service on 38 Mail-Express 
trains expanding passengers’ access to 
safe drinking water, through a digital 
ordering system.
Internet Ticketing generated a revenue 
of ₹1,536 crore approx., registering 
year-on-year growth of 7.66%. E-Tickets 
now account for 88.74% of reserved 
railway ticket bookings. This reflects 
how deeply our internet ticketing 
platform has become embedded in 
India’s travel ecosystem. Th

Daily Ticket Bookings increased to 
14.5 lakh with a record 18.40 lakh

Rail Ticket Booking Mobile App - IRCTC 
Rail Connect crossed 17.71 crore

Beyond train ticketing, IRCTC’s own 
Travel Platform – www.irctctourism.
com has evolved into a comprehensive 
Travel Services Hub, enabling 
passengers to manage their end-
to-end journeys through a single 
digital interface. 
Tourism delivered another year 
of robust growth, with revenue 
increasing by 19.49% to ₹890 crore, 
while profit grew by an impressive 
35.90%. Our portfolio of Bharat Gaurav 
Tourist Trains, luxury rail journeys, 
and pilgrimage circuits witness

launched the North East Discovery

Integrated Rail-Based Travel across

Building a Connected Travel 
Ecosystem
Our digital infrastructure continued to 
scale in line with growing passenger 
demand. The Next Generation 
e-Ticketing platform achieved peak 
processing capacity of over 37,000 
tickets per minute, strengthening 
reliability during periods of high 
demand. Aadhaar-authenticated 
Tatk

d peak 
processing capacity of over 37,000 
tickets per minute, strengthening 
reliability during periods of high 
demand. Aadhaar-authenticated 
Tatkal bookings also gained traction, 
with adoption increasing from 
6.77% to 17.74%, thereby enhancing 
booking security.
Our co-branded RuPay credit card 
programmes with SBI, Bank of Baroda, 
HDFC Bank, and RBL Bank generated 
revenue of ₹52.33 crore, reflecting 
year-on-year growth of 18% and 
deepening passenger engagement 
beyond the rail journey.
Advancing Responsible and 
Inclusive Growth
Our business streams bring with 
them a clear responsibility to use 
resources more thoughtfully and 
contribute meaningfully to the 
communities we serve.
At Rail Neer Plants, we have put in 
place structured systems for plastic 
waste collection and recycling under 
our Extended Producer Responsibility 
framework. Our plants also utilise 
solar evaporation ponds, rainwater 
harvesting, and water recycling systems 
to manage water responsibly, with

ty 
framework. Our plants also utilise 
solar evaporation ponds, rainwater 
harvesting, and water recycling systems 
to manage water responsibly, with 
120 KW of installed solar capacity 
across three facilities supporting 
cleaner production.
Our responsibility extends well beyond 
our operations. During the year, we 
supported the creation of a sustainable 
solid waste management ecosystem in 
Kinnaur in partnership with the Healing 
Himalayas Foundation, contributed to 
school nutrition through the Akshaya 
Patra Mid-Day Meal Programme, and 
strengthened access to preventive 
healthcare in communities around 
our operations.
Creating a Smile at Every 
Mile
India is travelling more, exploring more, 
and expecting more from every journey. 
For IRCTC, this presents a broader 
canvas that calls for stronger digital 
platforms, wider tourism offerings, 
and a consistently superior passenger 
experience. Our focus is to stay ahead 
of these evolving expectations by 
leveraging our reach,

m offerings,

experience. Our focus is to stay ahead 
of these evolving expectations by 
leveraging our reach, technology, and 
capabilities to create value across every 
mile of India’s growing travel economy.
As we pursue these opportunities, 
the principles by which we conduct 
our business will remain equally 
important. At IRCTC, we firmly believe 
that robust Corporate Governance is 
the cornerstone of sustainable value 
creation and long-term stakeholder 
trust. Guided by the principles of 
integrity, transparency, accountability, 
and ethical conduct, your Company 
remains steadfastly committed to 
maintaining the highest benchmarks

relevant regulations and applicable 
laws. We continuously refine our 
internal oversight, risk management 
frameworks, and disclosure practices 
to ensure that administrative growth 
and digital innovation go hand in 
hand with institutional responsibility,

I thank every member of Team IRCTC 
for the commitment they bring to this 
organization each day. I also express my 
sincere appreciation to our passengers, 
shareholders, business partners, and all 
other stakeholders for the continued 
trust they repose in IRCTC. Together, 
we will continue to serve a nation on 
the move and build an IRCTC that is 
ready for the journeys ahead.
Warm Regards,
Rahul Himalian

About Us
Creating Value Across the 
Travel Ecosystem
Indian Railway Catering and Tourism Corporation Ltd. (IRCTC), a 
Navratna Central Public Sector Enterprise under the Ministry of 
Railways, Government of India, serves as the hospitality, tourism 
and online ticketing arm of Indian Railways. By integrating digital 
platforms, catering, tourism and travel services, we have created a 
comprehensive ecosystem that enhances convenience and enriches 
the travel experience for millions of passengers.
Since 1999, our journey has evolved 
in step with India's rapidly expanding 
railway network and the nation's 
growing mobility aspirations. Guided 
by innovation, operational excellence 
and a customer-first approach, we have 
expanded our capabilities, building 
an integrated travel platform that 
supports seamless journeys while 
contributing to the growth of India's 
travel and tourism economy.

services, enhancing the overall passenger experience.

Point of Sale (POS) Handheld Billing Machines:
To curb overcharging and promote transparency, IRCTC has 
made billing through POS machines mandatory across its catering 
network. The system ensures issuance of invoices for every 
transaction, strengthens accounting and financial controls, and 
supports cashless transactions in line with the Government of 
India’s Digital India initiative.
As on March 31, 2026, 4,384 POS machines were deployed in 
951 pantry car rakes, 4,517 POS machines in 1,193 TSV train rakes, 
and 574 POS machines across 574 static catering units, including 
Refreshment Rooms, Jan Ahaars, Food Plazas, Fast Food Units, 
Retiring Rooms, Executive Lounges, and RYN/BNR Hotels under 
the IRCTC network.

g) Tatkal Scheme for Reserved Tickets: The Tatkal charges 
have been fixed as a percentage of fares at the rate of 10% 
of the basic fare for second class and 30% of the basic fare 
for all other classes subject to minimum and maximum limits. 
Tatkal tickets are issued for the actual distance of travel, 
instead of end-to-end, subject to the distance restrictions 
applicable to the train. The same Tatkal berth/seat may 
be booked in multiple legs till preparation of the charts. 
At the time of preparation of charts, the unutilised ones 
are released to the General RAC/Waiting list passengers. 
Tatkal booking opens at 10 AM for AC Classes and 11 AM 
for Non-AC Classes for normal users. Tatkal tickets can 
be booked one day in advance from the train originating 
station excluding the date of journey of enroute stations. 
The scheme is available on www.irctc.co.in and IRCTC Rail 
Connect Mobile App where customers can book tickets on 
the Tatkal scheme seamlessly.

h) VIKALP Scheme: Travellers who have been put on the 
waiting list, irrespective of a booking quota or concessions, 
can choose maximum five trains under this scheme. 
It does not confirm a berth, since it depends on the 
availability of seats in the given train. There is no refund 
or extra fare charged for these changed trains, including 
the Tatkal prices. Either all passengers of a PNR opting for 
this scheme will be transferred to alternate trains in the 
same class or none will. Once confirmed in an alternate 
train, the cancellation charges apply as per the usual 
rules. A person can be transferred to any train available 
within the window as per selection made by the user. The 
train list once selected under VIKALP can be changed or 
updated only once.

i) Same Day Online Refund: IRCTC continues to focus on 
enhancing customer experience and convenience for 
reserved rail e-tickets through its Website and Rail Connect 
Mobile App, with a core objective of strengthening 
customer retention. Accordingly, addressing payment 
and refund issues has been a key priority for us, as 
these have historically generated the largest number of 
customer complaints.
 Previously, refunds were processed using a traditional file-
based method, typically initiated on the next day (T+1) after 
a transaction. To improve efficiency and reduce customer 
grievances arising from delayed or failed transactions, 
IRCTC has implemented the *Same Day Refund Initiation 
API*. This functionality ensures that in cases of failed 
online rail e-ticket transactions—where a user’s account is 
debited but the ticket is not booked—the refund is initiated 
on the *same day* of the transaction, as soon as received 
by the Bank

 The first phase of this process was launched in*December 
2023*. Following this, with effect from *7 th August 2024*, 
IRCTC has extended same-day refunds to include *user-
cancelled tickets* and *waitlist drop tickets*, ensuring that 
refunds for all cancelled tickets are processed on the 
same day. Additionally, transactions made through *UPI, 
Credit card on UPI, Credit Line on UPI and WALLET* are 
now automatically refunded to users’ accounts on the 
same day, as soon as received by the Banks/Payment 
Gateways/Payment Aggregators.

technology to enhance customer satisfaction and 
streamline financial processes.

Advanced Manufacturing Process:
Rail Neer’s manufacturing infrastructure is designed to ensure 
maximum hygiene, precision, and efficiency:
Water Purification:
Water is drawn from borewells/Dam/Pipeline Water from 
state Government and undergoes an eight-stage purification 
process, which includes:
1. Activated carbon filtration Stage 1 & 2 – Stage 1 removes 
dust, dead microbes, odour/colour and stage 2 is for 
removing pesticides.
2. Auto Softening - Hardness of water is removed.
Statutory Reports
79

3. Ultra filtration - Colloidal, suspended particles and 
pyrogenic species are filtered out through Ultra 
Filtration membranes.
4. Reverse osmosis - All dissolved impurities are removed. 
Anti scaling agent not used. (All competitors use it to 
enhances membrane life)
5. Marble chip/ Calcite filtration - To boost "pH" - Exclusive 
process adopted by Rail Neer.
7. UV sterilization - UV-light causes change in the genetic 
material of micro organisms and thus prevents them 
from reproducing.
8. Ozonation- Water comes in contact with ozone gas for 
final disinfection from the micro organisms. The nascent 
oxygen is powerful oxidizing agent and kills the microbes.
6. Two-stage micron filtration - Impurities with size more 
than 0.2 micron are filtered out.

Indian Economic Overview
India’s economy maintained a strong growth trajectory during FY 
2025-26. Growth was driven by resilient domestic consumption, 
improving industrial performance and Government-led policy 
initiatives. Real GDP growth increased to 7.7% in FY 2025-26 1 
from 7.1% in FY 2024-25. 2 This reflects sustained economic 
momentum and macroeconomic stability. The services sector 
remained a major contributor to economic growth. Trade, 
repair, hotels and transport services grew by 10.1% in FY 
2025-26. Growth was further supported by infrastructure 
investments and improving business activity. Capacity creation 
and development initiatives strengthened overall economic 
expansion. India continued to rank among the fastest-growing 
major economies globally.

demand. Private consumption and investment were the

Economic growth was supported by resilient domestic 
demand. Private consumption and investment were the 
primary growth engines. Supportive financial conditions further 
aided momentum. Government infrastructure spending also 
contributed meaningfully. Growth remained broad-based across 
services and manufacturing sectors. Investment-led expansion 
continued throughout the year.
Inflationary pressures moderated during the year. CPI inflation

price stability. Monetary conditions remained accommodative.

Company Overview
Indian Railway Catering and Tourism Corporation Limited (IRCTC) 
is a Government of India enterprise under the administrative 
control of the Ministry of Railways. The Company provides 
catering, hospitality, internet ticketing, tourism and packaged 
drinking water services across the Indian Railways network. 
Established on 27 September 1999, IRCTC was incorporated 
to enhance professionalism, efficiency and service delivery in 
railway catering and tourism.
Over the years, IRCTC has evolved into a diversified tr

to enhance professionalism, efficiency and service delivery in 
railway catering and tourism.
Over the years, IRCTC has evolved into a diversified travel 
and hospitality service provider. Its operations span four key 
business segments: Catering and Hospitality, Internet Ticketing, 
Travel and Tourism and Packaged Drinking Water under the 
‘Rail Neer’ brand.
The Company plays an important role in supporting Indian 
Railways through onboard catering services, e-ticketing, 
tourism packages, luxury tourist trains, executive lounges, 
food plazas and digital travel services. IRCTC operates one of 
India’s largest online railway ticketing platforms. The platform 
provides technology-enabled booking solutions to millions of 
passengers across the country.

Tatkal Scheme for Reserved Tickets
The Tatkal Scheme enables passengers to book tickets for 
urgent travel needs. The facility is available across most 
reserved classes on Indian Railways trains.
Tatkal bookings open one day before the train's scheduled 
departure from the originating station, excluding the journey 
date. Bookings commence at 10:00 AM for AC classes and 
11:00 AM for non-AC classes. Passengers can book Tatkal 
tickets through the IRCTC website and the IRCTC Rail Connect 
application. Confirmed Tatkal tickets can be cancelled but are 
not eligible for refunds. Waitlisted Tatkal tickets are eligible for 
cancellation and refund, subject to applicable rules. Additionally, 
Indian Railways continued enhancing the Tatkal booking system 
through digital initiatives and system improvements. These

VIKALP Scheme
The VIKALP (Alternate Train Accommodation Scheme) provides 
confirmed accommodation to waitlisted passengers. Under the 
scheme, eligible passengers may receive seats in alternate trains 
operating on the same route and date, subject to availability. 
The scheme improves passenger convenience and optimises 
berth utilisation across the railway network. VIKALP is available 
free of cost to passengers booking through IRCTC platforms. 
No additional fare is charged for availing the facility. Passengers 
receive SMS notifications regarding the allotment of alternate 
accommodation. The scheme reduces inconvenience arising 
from waitlisted tickets while improving occupancy management 
and reservation efficiency across Indian Railways.

Packaged drinking water
IRCTC provides packaged drinking water under the brand name 
of Rail Neer. It is processed, purified and bottled at IRCTC plants, 
which undergo rigorous multi-stage purification processes, 
including reverse osmosis, ultraviolet treatment and ozonation. 
These steps remain essential to ensure that the product meets 
the stringent quality standards set by the Bureau of Indian 
Standards (BIS). Rail Neer maintains an exclusive position in 
the supply of packaged drinking water across Indian Railways, 
ensuring quality and continuity in service. The brand operates 
20 advanced production units and currently fulfills 60–70% of 
the existing demand across trains and stations.

of a previous night, that was a military action by India against

Due to the cancellation of our return flights , my family and I

reached Hyderabad.
The Leh-Manali leg was the most thrilling part of our trip. The 
supposedly 12-hour road journey stretched to 16 hours as we 
navigated treacherous, snow-covered Himalayan roads. We 
drove across frozen rivers, unpaved single-lane tracks and 
narrow mountain passes. There were landslides, road repairs,

and seizure vide order dated 27.4.2022 and stay is continuing. No further date has been fixed in this matter as yet. Since, the

General description of the defined benefit schemes/defined contribution scheme:
(i) Gratuity: Payable on separation @ 15 days pay for each completed year of service to eligible employees who render 
continuous service of 5 years or more. The gratuity ceiling of H20 Lakhs has been considered for actuarial valuation. Actuarial 
valuation though was made for all employees irrespective of the completion of 5 years of service.
(ii) Leave Encashment: Leave salary is provided for based on valua

gh was made for all employees irrespective of the completion of 5 years of service.
(ii) Leave Encashment: Leave salary is provided for based on valuations, as at the balance sheet date, made by independent 
actuary for present value of obligation without netting of fair value of plan assets.
(iii) Half Pay Leave: to eligible employees who have accumulated half pay leaves. Half pay leave is provided for based on 
actuarial valuations, as at the balance sheet date.
(iv) Leave Travel Concession(LTC) : to eligible employees is provided for based on actuarial valuations, as at the balance sheet date.
(v) Provident Fund: 12% of the Basic Pay plus Dearness Allowance of Employees and equivalent Contribution of the Corporation 
is contributed to the Provident Fund maintained with the Regional Provident Fund Commissioner, New Delhi. Corporation’s 
contribution to provident fund is charged to revenue.
(vi) Foreign Service Contribution: Foreign service contribution payable for leave salary and pe

contribution to provident fund is charged to revenue.
(vi) Foreign Service Contribution: Foreign service contribution payable for leave salary and pension in respect of deputationists 
(employees who have joined the corporation on deputation for a fixed period from Indian Railways or other government 
organizations) in terms of Government rules and regulations, is charged to revenue on accrual basis.
(vii) National Pension Scheme: Retirement benefits in the form of NPS is a defined contribution scheme. The company has no 
obligation, other than the contribution @10% of Basic pay plus dearness allowance payable under such scheme. The company 
recognize contribution payable to such scheme as an expense for the employees while in service.
(viii) Post Retirement Medical Benefit (PRMB): To eligible retired employees, provided for based on actuarial valuation as at the 
Balance sheet date.

rendered by the company, organization structure & internal reporting system and has identified four reportable segments of its 
business as follows:-

The corporation caters mainly to the needs of the domestic market. As such there are no reportable geographical segments.
The accounting principles used in the preparation of the Standalone financial statements is consistently applied to record revenue 
& expenditure in individual segments, as set out in the note of material accounting policies.
Revenue and direct expenses in relation to segment are allocated based on items that are individually identifiable to the respective 
segment while the remainder of the costs are allocated to all segments on proportionate basis. The management

are summarized below:-

ments.

contractual obligations, and arises principally from the Company’s receivables from customers. The company is exposed to 
credit risk from its financial activities including trade receivable, deposits with banks, financial institutions and other financial 
instruments. The maximum exposure to credit risk is equal to the carrying value of the financial assets. The objective of

counterparties, taking into account their financial position, past ex

vent losses in financial assets. The Company assesses the credit quality of the

d) Liquidity risk

manages its liquidity risk by ensuring , as far as possible, that it will always have sufficient liquidity to meet its liabilities when 
due, under both normal and stressed conditions, without incurring unacceptable losses or risk to the company's reputation.
 The company's principal sources of liquidity are cash and cash equivalents and the cash flow that is generated from

Note :- 57 Financial Risk Management
The Group’s principal financial liabilities comprise trade and other payables. The main purpose of these financial liabilities is to 
finance the Group’s operations and to provide guarantees to support its operation. The Group’s principal financial assets include 
trade and other receivables and cash and cash equivalents that derive directly from its operations.
The Group is exposed to market risk, credit risk and liquidity risk. The Group financial risk activities are governed by appropriate 
policies and procedures and that financial risk are identified, measured and managed in accordance with the companies policies and 
risk objectives. The board of directors reviews and agrees policies for managing each of these risk, which are summarized below:-
a) Market Risk

market prices

market prices. Market risk comprises Interest rate risk and foreign currency risk. Financial instruments affected by market risk 
includes security deposits, Bank deposits and other non derivative financial instruments.
 i) Interest Rate Risk
 Interest rate risk is the risk that the fair value of future cash flows of a financial instruments will fluctuate because of 
change in market interest rate. The Group manages its interest risk in accordance with the companies policies and risk 
objective. Financial instruments affected by interest rate risk includes deposits with banks. Interest rate risk on these 
financial instruments are very low as interest rate is for the period of financial instruments.

Foreign Currency Risk
 The Group operates internationally. In view of low volume of foreign currency transactions, no material exposure exists 
from foreign currency risk arising form foreign currency transactions. Group does not hedge any foreign currency risk.
b) Credit risk
 Credit risk is the risk of financial loss to the Group if a customer or counterparty to a financial instrument fails to meet 
its contractual obligations, and arises principally from the Group’s receivables from customers. The Group is exposed to 
credit risk from its financial activities including trade receivable, deposits with banks, financial institutions and other financial 
instruments. The maximum exposure to credit risk is equal to the carrying value of the financial assets. The objective of 
managing counterparty credit risk is to prevent losses in financial assets. The Group assesses the credit quality of the 
counterparties, taking into account their financial position, past experience and other fact

d) Liquidity risk
 Liquidity risk is the risk that the Group will not be able to meet its financial obligations as they become due. The Group 
manages its liquidity risk by ensuring , as far as possible, that it will always have sufficient liquidity to meet its liabilities when 
due, under both normal and stressed conditions, without incurring unacceptable losses or risk to the Group's reputation.

within next financial year.
a) Fair valuation measurement and valuation process
 The fair values of financial assets and financial liabilities are measured using the valuation techniques including DCF model. 
The inputs to these methods are taken from observable markets where possible, but where this it is not feasible, a degree of 
judgement is required in arriving at fair values. Judgements include considerations of inputs such as liquidity risk, credit risk 
and volatility. Changes in assumptions about these factors could affect the reported fair value of financial instruments.
b) Taxes
 Deferred tax assets are recognized to the extent that it is probable that taxable profit will be available against w

financial instruments.
b) Taxes
 Deferred tax assets are recognized to the extent that it is probable that taxable profit will be available against which losses 
can be utilized Significant management judgement is required to determine the amount of deferred tax asset that can be 
recognized, based upon the likely timing and level of future taxable profit together with future tax planning strategies.
c) Defined benefit Obligations
 Employee benefit obligations are determined using actuarial valuations. An actuarial valuation involves making various 
assumptions that may differ from actual developments in the future. These include the determination of the discount rate, 
future salary increases and mortality rates. Due to the complexities involved in the valuation and its long term nature, a defined 
benefit obligation is highly sensitive to changes in these assumptions. All assumptions are reviewed at each reporting date

viz., the Code on Wages, 2019; the Code on Social Security, 2020; the Industrial Relations Code, 2020; and the Occupational 
Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code, 2020 (collectively referred to as the ""New Labour Codes""). These New Labour 
Codes were notified by the Government on November 21, 2025.
The Ministry of Labour & Employment published Central Rules and FAQs to enable assessment of the financial impact due to 
changes in regulations. The Group has assessed the impact of these changes with the best availa

changes in regulations. The Group has assessed the impact of these changes with the best available information and guidance 
provided by the Institute of Chartered Accountants of India (‘ICAI’). The impact of these changes is not material on the financial 
statements. The Group continues to monitor the finalisation of State Rules and clarifications from the Government on other aspects 
of the Labour Codes and would provide appropriate accounting effect as and when such clarifications are issued/ rules are 
notified. However, an mount of H 60.08 lakhs have been provided by the Company for the period from 21/11/2025 to 31/03/2026
